title: Cadence Finance renewal & capacity top-up — Asia edge readout

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-16 16:00 UTC — Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Sanjay Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Lena Morris (Cadence Head of ML), Tomás Rivera (Cadence Platform), Aisha Khan (Cadence Security), Paul Nguyen (Cadence Finance)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough): customer is leaning to renew with a top-up, wants asia edge and a short private pilot. some security/finance items to clear.

[00:00] Sanjay Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick check-in today — do a short readout from our side on the APAC pilot, then go through renewal numbers.
[00:22] Lena Morris: yep, hi all. we ran the internal perf with the staging dataset, saw latency in tokyo node at around 70 to 90 ms median, which is good but we want to validate in a private-ish context.
[00:35] Maya Chen: right, the tokyo edge test used a lightweight model variant, quantized; the numbers we saw were consistent with the bench sheet, but there was some jitter under burst — likely batching config and network egress.
[00:48] Tomás Rivera: jitter as in queueing? we saw a couple 300 ms spikes during synthetic bursts.
[00:56] Maya Chen: yeah, the synthetic burst exposed a KV cash miss — sorry KV cache miss — when prefix caching didn't hit. we can tune cache TTL and also adjust batching policy to prefer latency SLO over throughput.
[01:12] Aisha Khan: before we go deep, quick sec: security is the gating factor. we need KMS integration notes, proof of audit logs being immutable, and a clear data residency statement for tokens logged.
[01:26] Sanjay Patel: absolutely, we'll send the SOC 2 package and our KMS playbook. Maya, can you call out the KMS integration path for the private pilot?
[01:35] Maya Chen: for private pilot we recommend customer-managed KMS via a shared HSM setup or cloud KMS; we support both. there might be a short auth handshake; for the on-prem package we can provide guidance on key rotation.
[01:49] Lena Morris: good. on renewal numbers: Paul's looking at budget windows for the fiscal Q3. Paul?
[01:56] Paul Nguyen: yeah, finance side: if we renew at current committed capacity + 30% top-up for APAC burst, what's the incremental cost and do we get any pilot credits? also curious about monthly true-up flexibility.
[02:12] Sanjay Patel: we can do two proposals: a straight top-up with tiered discounts, or a committed-plus-pilot model where we add a short private pilot with a one-time pilot credit. i'll put both in the sheet.
[02:25] Paul Nguyen: sounds good. do you have an example of the pilot credit structure?
[02:29] Sanjay Patel: typically 6-8 weeks pilot, 25-50% credit on pilot consumption depending on commitment. we'll model with numbers.
[02:40] Tomás Rivera: technical question: dedicated capacity vs private pilot — can we run the pilot in our VPC and still use Redwood's control plane? we need to know data plane boundaries.
[02:52] Maya Chen: yes — for VPC/private deployment we split control plane and data plane: control plane is Redwood-managed, and data plane sits in your VPC or on-prem. logs can be routed to your SIEM; we can also disable token retention at rest.
[03:07] Aisha Khan: disable token retention? important — we need evidence of that. also need the retention defaults and how to opt out.
[03:14] Maya Chen: default retention is 30 days for pilot telemetry unless disabled; for Private we can configure 0 retention and stream logs directly to your Kinesis/Splunk endpoint.
[03:26] Lena Morris: there's another concern — latency SLA. our customer-facing tooling expects p50 < 120 ms in APAC. do you commit to SLOs for edge nodes?
[03:36] Sanjay Patel: for Dedicated/APAC nodes we provide SLA-backed latency targets in the contract; for pilots we provide performance expectations but not full SLA until Dedicated is in place.
[03:46] Tomás Rivera: ok, that makes sense. we need a playbook for migrating from pilot to Dedicated once proven.
[03:53] Maya Chen: we'll include a migration checklist: capacity handoff, traffic cutover, DNS and routing, KV cache warmup, and a small canary for 2% of traffic for 48 hours.
[04:06] Paul Nguyen: on billing — if we commit now for a 12-month uplift, can we get price protection for exchange rate fluctuations for invoices in JPY?
[04:16] Sanjay Patel: yes we can add an FX protection clause for customers with multi-currency invoicing; i'll include options in pricing sheet.
[04:23] Lena Morris: quick competitor note — we've also been talking to EdgeServe and CloudGiant AI about Japan nodes, they quoted lower baseline cost but didn't offer the private KMS flow we need.
[04:37] Sanjay Patel: understood — we tend to compete on operations and compliance rather than raw list price.
[04:44] Tomás Rivera: on integration effort: how much engineering time do you estimate for the VPC pilot?
[04:51] Maya Chen: for a standard VPC/private pilot, 2-3 full-time engineer-weeks from your side for connectors, plus one Redwood SE week for runbook and cutover. if you want an on-prem package it's more.
[05:04] Tomás Rivera: that's reasonable. can you provide a stub runbook we can review?
[05:08] Maya Chen: yes, action item: i'll share an APAC edge runbook and the preliminary perf deck.
[05:13] Lena Morris: on success criteria — our ML team wants: (1) p50 < 120ms, (2) <1% 5xxs during peak, (3) no persistent KV cache cold starts during steady state.
[05:26] Maya Chen: we can monitor all three and set up regression alerts tied to the eval set you supplied. also we'll suggest quantization profile adjustments if quality dips.
[05:36] Aisha Khan: security again — we need an architecture diagram showing where audit logs live, who has access, and the immutability chain of custody.
[05:45] Sanjay Patel: we'll produce that. i'll include the SOC2 control mappings as well.
[05:51] Paul Nguyen: timeline question: we'd like the pilot to start in the last week of July and run through mid-September, aligned to our marketing campaign. is that doable?
[06:03] Sanjay Patel: week of 7/27 is possible. assuming we sign paper and you share traffic profiles, Redwood can spin up the pilot nodes.
[06:12] Tomás Rivera: anything special for compliance in Japan? data sovereignty?
[06:18] Aisha Khan: we want logs to be kept in Japan region only for Japanese traffic; non-Japan logs can be US/EU.
[06:26] Maya Chen: we can route logs by region and configure storage region; there are some limitations for third-party SIEM connectors but we have patterns.
[06:36] Lena Morris: great. Paul's point on finance: will you include monthly true-up flexibility? we might overshoot early on.
[06:45] Sanjay Patel: yes, we have a true-up mechanism with a 30-day lookback and a small buffer tier to absorb initial bursts. i'll include it in the pricing doc.
[06:54] Paul Nguyen: ok. any blockers for getting PO out by end of July?
[06:59] Aisha Khan: security must sign off on KMS and audit flow; legal wants a limited indemnity check but nothing unusual.
[07:08] Sanjay Patel: understood. i'll coordinate with our legal ops.
[07:12] Tomás Rivera: can we get a short perf benchmark run from Redwood that mirrors our 50qps profile? last test used 10qps and wasn't representative.
[07:22] Maya Chen: yes, we can run a 50 qps synthetic with your recent prompt set; we'll run it in the tokyo staging node and include KV cache warmup steps.
[07:31] Lena Morris: please ensure we collect tail latency metrics; the business cares about the 95/99.
[07:36] Maya Chen: noted. we'll collect p50/p95/p99 and error breakdown by token type.
[07:43] Sanjay Patel: quick recap and next steps: i'll send updated pricing and include FX protection options and pilot credit scenarios; Maya will share runbook and perf deck; Cadence to share traffic and security contacts.
[07:55] Paul Nguyen: timeline recap — pricing and docs by 7/20, traffic heatmap by 7/21, pilot kickoff week of 7/27.
[08:03] Lena Morris: sounds good. any final Qs?
[08:07] Aisha Khan: one small ask — include retention toggles in the runbook so we can show the board we can set retention to zero.
[08:15] Maya Chen: yep, retention toggle doc will be included.
[08:19] Sanjay Patel: alright, we'll follow up. thanks everyone.

(Transcription notes: occasional word confusions: "KV cash" for KV cache, "on prem package" sometimes hyphenated, speaker labels approximate.)

Meeting end.
